summary: Air-gapped on-prem upgrade request: offline bundle delivery + signing/verification + maintenance window planning
body:
Request
HelioBank (enterprise, on-prem / air-gapped) is requesting an upgrade of their Redwood Private deployment using an offline (air-gapped) bundle. Support needs to confirm prerequisites, bundle delivery workflow, signing/verification expectations, and schedule/approval requirements for the maintenance window.

Customer context
- Deployment type: Redwood Private (on-prem, air-gapped)
- Connectivity: no outbound internet from cluster; limited inbound to admin bastion
- Upgrade driver: security patch + feature parity with hosted (customer requested "latest stable" that supports upgrade/rollback workflow)

Information needed from customer (blocking)
1) Current versions
   - Redwood Private release currently installed (control plane + runtime)
   - Helm chart versions (if pinned)
   - Kubernetes version / distro
2) Cluster + storage details
   - StorageClass names used by Redwood components
   - Snapshot capability (CSI snapshots supported? if not, confirm DB backup strategy)
   - Free disk space available on nodes and on any backup target
3) Offline registry / artifact import
   - Do they have an internal container registry available to the cluster?
   - Preferred import method (registry push vs node-level preload)
   - Any restrictions on image signing (cosign) / SBOM requirements
4) Cryptographic verification requirements
   - Does HelioBank require customer-held keys or will Redwood public verification keys be accepted?
   - Allowed hashing/signature algorithms (org policy)
5) Maintenance window
   - Desired maintenance window length and timezone
   - Required customer-side approvals/change-management gates
   - RTO expectation and acceptance of brief downtime during upgrade sequencing

Proposed Redwood approach (for customer validation)
- Provide an offline upgrade bundle including:
  - Signed manifest + checksums
  - Helm charts + values templates
  - Installer binary/package (signed)
  - Container images list + instructions to import to internal registry
- Run prechecks on-site (or via PS) prior to the change window.
- Take mandatory backups prior to applying changes; verify backups.
- Execute upgrade using installer "plan" + "apply" workflow; collect diagnostics bundle on completion.
- If any validation gate fails, abort and execute rollback per rollback policy (subject to forward-only migration guardrails).

Next steps
- Loop in Professional Services (Markus Klein / Bruno Silva) for on-site coordination and offline artifact handling.
- Confirm customer security requirements for signing key trust and verification behavior.
- Once requirements are received, Release Eng (Connor O’Brien) to propose target version and deliver offline bundle ETA.
comments: 2026-02-10 09:14 (Dev Patel, Support) — Created ticket after customer email requesting "offline upgrade package". Customer states: "cluster is air-gapped; we can accept media transfer via approved channel." Asked for current installed version + k8s details. Added Markus Klein as PS lead to coordinate.

2026-02-10 10:02 (Markus Klein, PS) — Acknowledged. We’ll need a formal upgrade questionnaire + planned window. HelioBank historically requires CAB approval; expect 7–10 business days lead time. I’ll set up a requirements call; please confirm who from Release Eng / Security should attend.

2026-02-10 10:11 (Dev Patel, Support) — Proposed attendees: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng) for bundle/versioning, Hanae Suzuki (signing implementation) or Marcus Lin (Security Eng) for key trust model. Shared draft questions: current versions, internal registry availability, snapshot support, and whether they require customer-held verification keys.

2026-02-11 14:27 (Marcus Lin, Security Eng) — For air-gapped: we can provide a signed manifest + checksum list and a verification command path in the installer. If customer requires customer-owned keys, we can discuss but it’s not the default. Please ask if they can trust Redwood public verification keys and whether they require SBOMs at import time.

2026-02-12 08:45 (Connor O’Brien, Release Eng) — FYI: offline bundle format is aligned with installer PR_439 (manifest parsing + signature verification). We should confirm they can import images into an internal registry reachable by the cluster. If not, we need an alternate path (node preload) and we should set expectations (slower, more error-prone).

2026-02-13 16:10 (Dev Patel, Support) — Sent customer questionnaire + requested a sample of their "approved media transfer" process. Also requested: timezone + tentative window length; and whether they require a staged rehearsal in a non-prod environment.

2026-02-17 11:03 (Markus Klein, PS) — Customer replied with partial info: they do have an internal registry, but want a list of image digests in advance for security scanning. They did not provide current Redwood version yet. They asked: "Can Redwood provide a single tarball with everything?" I told them yes conceptually (offline bundle) but we must still import images into their registry.

2026-02-18 09:26 (Dev Patel, Support) — Clarified to customer: offline bundle will include signed manifest + checksums; images can be delivered as tar archives suitable for `docker load`/`ctr images import` then pushed to internal registry, or provided as an OCI layout depending on their tooling. Requested they confirm preferred tooling (containerd vs docker) and OS constraints on their bastion.

2026-02-20 13:40 (Bruno Silva, PS) — Added note: for fully air-gapped, we should schedule a precheck run at least 48 hours before the window to catch storage class / snapshot permissions / disk space issues. Also ask whether they can provide a temporary "staging" namespace to rehearse chart rendering and image pulls from internal registry.

2026-02-24 17:05 (Dev Patel, Support) — Status set to Waiting on Customer. Blockers remain: (1) exact current Redwood Private version and Helm chart versions, (2) Kubernetes version/distro, (3) confirmation on signing trust model (Redwood public key acceptable?) and SBOM requirements, (4) requested maintenance window and required approvals. Once received, we will: propose target version + deliver offline bundle ETA + PS-led runbook for their change window.
